sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioner-accused seeking to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.6484 of 2020 on the file of learned XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Nampally, Hyderabad, registered for the offences under Sections 498A and 506 I.P.C. and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2.

entities.text:
XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Vempati Mallikarjun Shastry, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Srinivasa Rao Madiraju, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2 ETD,J 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that there are no specific allegations against the petitioner herein, who is the husband of respondent No.2-de facto complainant.
The only allegation against the petitioner is that he was saving money for their future, over which the de facto complainant is aggrieved.
He further submitted that the de facto complainant herself has necked out the petitioner from the house and has filed divorce O.P. against the petitioner herein.
In the cross-examination done in the divorce case, the de facto complainant has admitted about her cruel behaviour against the petitioner herein.
Even if the allegations are believed to be true, no complaint is lodged by the de facto complainant earlier alleging beating or harassment by the petitioner.
In fact, the de facto complainant herself is harassing the petitioner.
He, therefore, prayed to quash the proceedings in the present C.C. against the petitioner.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that the petitioner has harassed respondent No.2-de facto complainant in many ways by subjecting her to physical and mental harassment and further, he has neglected the children for the past six years.
He further submitted that though the petitioner claims that he is interested in the family life with respondent No.2, 3 ETD,J he has not filed any petition for restitution of conjugal rights.

Further, the statements of LWs.4 to 7, if perused,
reveal the harassment made by the petitioner herein.
He, therefore, prayed to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

5. Perused the record.
6.

Respondent No.2-de facto complainant alleges that from the day of her marriage with the petitioner, he has been spending both their salaries and has acquired properties in his name in Hyderabad, at their in-laws place and at Nizamabad Town.
Further, he used to send money to her in-laws for their maintenance and purchase of additional properties.

It is further alleged that the petitioner stopped spending on her and the children; that he never took care of their family needs;
and that for the past several years, he has been demanding her salary to be given to him without leaving minimum money required for maintenance of the house.

It is further alleged that whenever she resisted, she was subjected to physical assault and that the petitioner used to beat her till she become unconscious and several times she sustained internal injuries in abdomen and other private parts.
It is further alleged that the petitioner has 4 ETD,J been demanding additional dowry from her parents through her.
Though initially she heeded to his demands, she stopped later on and was subjected to physical assault.
It is alleged that she got crippled both mentally and physically due to the harassment meted out by the petitioner.

It is further alleged that when she expressed her inability to serve him and others invited by him to the house due to ill-health and during late nights,
she was assaulted.
Whenever she expressed her inability to serve them during late nights, she was beaten up.
The said harassment is also known to the maid servants of their house.

In the recent past,
the petitioner is into real estate business and as he required more and more money for purchase of open plots, he used to demand the same from her.
Though attempts were made by her parents for a peaceful living, her husband and in-laws were non- cooperative.
It is alleged that the petitioner used to regularly beat her, took away her salary and has been attempting to kill her.
7. Thus, the allegations prima facie point out the offences under Sections 498A and 506 I.P.C. and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against the petitioner herein.
LWs.6 and 7 are the independent witnesses apart from the de facto complainant and her family members.
The veracity of these 5 ETD,J witnesses needs to be tested during the course of trial.

Hence, it is deemed appropriate to dispense with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial Court.
8.

Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of dispensing with the attendance of the petitioner before the trial Court provided he is represented by a counsel before the trial Court on every date of hearing and shall appear before the trial Court whenever his presence is required during the course of trial.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
